                                         PROJECT NO. 58481

    RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                      § PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
    LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                   §
    STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                §            OF TEXAS

                                  COMMENTS OF EOLIAN, L.P.
                                ON PROPOSED NEW 16 TAC §25.194

         COMES NOW Eolian, L.P. (Eolian) and files these comments on proposed new 16 Texas

Administrative Code (TAC) §25.194, relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards. This

proposed new rule is intended to set forth the standards and gating criteria for new large load

customers seeking to reliably interconnect to the ERCOT transmission network in a manner that

supports business development in this state.

         Eolian is a Corporate Member of the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT)

and owns several certificated Power Generation Companies (PGCs) and ERCOT-registered

Resource Entities that operate Energy Storage Resources (ESRs or batteries) in the ERCOT

Region.     Eolian is also currently in the process of developing a domestic industrial metal

production facility that will have an expected peak demand that would qualify it as a “large load

customer” within the meaning of proposed §25.194. As a result, Eolian would be directly affected

by this proposed rule that sets forth a framework of standards for new large loads seeking to

interconnect to the ERCOT system and ERCOT’s batch study interconnection process.

         When it enacted Senate Bill 6 (SB 6) during its last Regular Session in 2025, the Texas

Legislature required the Commission to “establish standards for interconnecting large load

customers in the ERCOT power region in a manner designed to support business development in

this state while minimizing the potential for stranded infrastructure costs and maintaining system

reliability.”1    This proposed rule is intended to implement that statutory requirement.


1
     Texas Utilities Code §37.0561(b).
 Unfortunately, while §25.194, as proposed, might “minimiz[e] the potential for stranded

infrastructure costs and maintain[] system reliability”, it fails to “support business development in

this state”, at least to the extent that industrial facilities whose purpose is to reduce the United

States’ reliance on imports of critical metals will be burdened by financial requirements and have

the potential for significant power limitations.

        Eolian appreciates that ERCOT is facing a tremendous demand to interconnect large data

center loads. According to ERCOT’s Preliminary Long-Term Load Forecast (LTLF) for 2026-

2032,2 256,474 MW of its 367,790 MW LTLF Peak Demand plus TSP RFI Submissions for 2032

is comprised of medium loads and large loads (25+ MW).3 Of the Large Loads by Load Type,

94% are data center loads.4 As a result, it is not surprising that much of the focus of this

rulemaking, and much of the focus on Planning Guide Revision Request (PGRR) 145, Batch Zero

Process for Large Load Interconnections, has been on addressing the interconnection of data

centers. However, not all large loads are data centers – 2.3% of the Large Loads by Load Type are

Industrial (including Hydrogen/E-Fuels) and Oil and Gas (Chemical Refining, Production, and

Processing). Eolian anticipates that domestic industrial metal production facilities would be

included in this 2.3%.

        A domestic industrial metal production facility does not fit neatly within the current

structure of §25.194, as proposed, much less PGRR 145 as it is currently being developed by

ERCOT. But, regardless, this type of facility would be subject to the Commission’s proposed large

load interconnection standards in proposed §25.194 and ERCOT’s batch study interconnection

process in PGRR 145. Specifically, the development timeline and economics of this facility are


2
    Project No. 58777, Triennial Reliability Assessment for the ERCOT Region under §25.508, Preliminary Long-
    Term Forecast for Years 2026 – 2032 (April 15, 2026).
3
    Id.at 2.
4
    Id. at 4.

                                                                                 Eolian Comments - Page 2
 not compatible with the non-refundability of financial security and non-refundable interconnection

fee requirements that are currently in proposed §25.194. The facility’s development timeline and

economics are also not compatible with ERCOT’s proposed plan to impose a load ramping

schedule of its choice through the batch study interconnection process on large load customers that

are not determined to be “Base Load not Subject to Additional Study”.5 Therefore, it is imperative

that the financial security requirements in proposed §25.194(d)(10) be revised to provide that the

financial security posted is fully refundable after paying applicable costs. In addition, the potential

application of proposed subsection (h), Non-utilized capacity, to a domestic industrial metal

production facility when it is under construction and subsequently starting production may

preclude the facility developer’s ability to finance the project in the first place. While financial

institutions will understand the potential for development delays associated with a complex

industrial manufacturing facility, the potential that construction and initial operational delays could

result in the revocation of interconnection capacity and non-refundability of the majority of posted

financial security and a non-refundable interconnection fee, as currently proposed in §25.194, may

be viewed as too high of a risk to finance the industrial project.

        Eolian anticipates that the Commission will modify proposed §25.194 in response to the

significant number of stakeholder comments that it already has and will receive in this rulemaking

project. As the Commission considers additional rule changes, Eolian respectfully requests that

the Commission consider how its potential rule revisions will impact a domestic industrial metal

production facility that is needed to address critical U.S. security issues and whether this facility

will be able to locate in the ERCOT region under the Commission’s large load interconnection

standards framework and ERCOT’s batch study interconnection process.



5
    See PGRR 145, Section 9.2.1.1.

                                                                             Eolian Comments - Page 3
  Respectfully submitted,



        /s/ Aaron Zubaty
           Aaron Zubaty
 Chief Executive Officer
            Eolian, L.P.
aaron@eolianenergy.com
         (650) 744-2100


          April 17, 2026
